papers.abstract: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. However, it is unknown how dedicated training of these networks can contribute to the successes of weight-space programming. We present a benchmark of LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, in which five LLMs edit convolutional networks and vision transformers on relabeling and error-correction tasks on Waterbirds, CIFAR-100, PACS and Entity-30. We report more than 2,600 such edit processes, whereby each edit is scored on held-out images for success, side effects and accuracy loss. We compare standard training with label smoothing, gradient-based editable training, and our Edit-Ready Training (ERT), a novel method that rehearses the direct, closed-form weight edits LLMs perform. We show...

papers.title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models have greatly improved input understanding in universal multimodal embedding models. However, this understanding does not ensure that their embeddings preserve the evidence needed to distinguish relevant items from confusable alternatives. To preserve essential discriminative evidence in embeddings, this paper proposes DiLE, a discrimination-aware latent-space learning framework that combines task guidance with on-policy retrieval feedback. Specifically, a few learnable queries are used to encode task-relevant information in a compact latent space. Reasoning instructions and auxiliary answer-generation supervision shape these representations to support both task understanding and retrieval discrimination. To address task-specific discriminative needs, we design shared-private expert adaptation that integrates cross-task knowledge...

papers.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
papers.abstract: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operate offline. In this paper, we study online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric videos. Using only observed video, task instructions, and prior predictions, our model identifies and localizes completed action attempts and classifies them as correct, modified, slip, corrections, or additions; omitted steps are determined after the video ends. We compare a modular pipeline, with separate step identification, temporal localization, and execution...

papers.title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
papers.abstract: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. Once installed, the new capabilities run independently of the language model. Given a grammar or eight demonstrations, weight programs enable previously unseen command compositions (0% to 99.8% exact match) and a new pickup action (0% to 98.4% success), while preserving the original...

papers.title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging. Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution. Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety. To address these challenges, we introduce State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response. SAFI comprises two stages, (1) fallback target construction, which assigns stationary arm commands and consistent gripper targets...

papers.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
papers.abstract: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic...

papers.title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
papers.abstract: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement...

papers.title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
papers.abstract: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. Despite their architectural differences, these methods all share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into a latent space and only then modeled by the generator. We take a different route and propose Direct3D-V3, a latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that discards the VAE altogether and operates in the native voxel domain, directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling. To make this direct voxel formulation geometrically reliable, we introduce an implicit manifold regularization over neighboring voxels to suppress non-watertight surfaces, and convert predicted SDF...

papers.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
papers.abstract: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid (>250times dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width...

papers.title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object. Existing approaches typically rely on full observation histories, which become redundant over long horizons, or text summaries, which may omit precise visual details. We study visual moment memory, the ability to retain such details from key moments for subsequent manipulation. To support this study, we introduce VMBench, a suite of long-horizon manipulation tasks requiring memory of spatial locations, visual appearances, and their associations. We further propose MomentMem, a hierarchical architecture in which a VLM-based memorizer selects keyframes and an executor predicts actions conditioned on the selected memories. This separation enables us to evaluate memory selection alongside closed-loop task success and to study...

papers.title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
papers.abstract: Agent skills are documents in which experts write down procedural knowledge, and models increasingly maintain them by rewriting them without feedback. Such rewriting could adapt a skill to the model that uses it or erode the expert knowledge that makes it useful, yet how skills evolve under this feedback-free self-evolution has not been studied. We let models rewrite expert skills round after round without any task, run or judgment and run agents built on the same models with the rewritten skills. Our experiments show that the skills lose value rather than improve, as every model we test performs worse with them on every benchmark, by 15 points on average on SkillsBench after thirty rounds. Sampling each model's prior with skills it writes from the topic alone, we find that rewriting pulls skills toward this prior and gives up first the knowledge outside it....

papers.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
papers.abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are increasingly deployed with access to search tools at inference. Yet pretraining remains predominantly focused on predicting static text, with search capabilities typically introduced during post-training. We propose Search-Native Pretraining as a practical route to teach search capability during pretraining from ordinary text corpora. Specifically, we augment pretraining corpus at scale with web-search queries and retrieve web response using a local index. Training on this augmented corpus teaches models to generate search calls and incorporate retrieved evidence during language modeling. Across Wikipedia and DCLM-Edu corpora and 360M to 3.3B parameter scales, search-pretrained models ("QueryLM") show improved performance on knowledge-intensive tasks and higher steerability toward the retrieved evidence. Crucially, their advantage...

papers.title: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. Existing curation methods typically infer data value from intrinsic sample properties or training-dependent proxies that do not measure downstream policy utility. To address this, we introduce Policy-Aware Data Valuation (PAD), a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. PAD combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients and a regularized approximation of local training geometry, producing scalable influence-based values for the policy. A controlled group-removal study establishes the directional...

papers.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
papers.abstract: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the...

papers.title: Prism: Hierarchical Text Detection with Minimalist Design
papers.abstract: Hierarchical text detection aims to localize words, text lines, and paragraphs while parsing their structural relationships. It provides essential structural cues for visual text understanding. To maximize accuracy, existing methods typically rely on complex multi-scale feature fusion necks and heavy-weight heads, resulting in bloated architectures and low inference efficiency. In this paper, we argue that a sufficiently pre-trained backbone can effectively replace these sophisticated external modules, while simple geometric inclusion suffices for hierarchical text structural parsing. Thus, we propose Prism, a minimalist framework for hierarchical text detection. Prism performs multi-granularity detection by attaching parallel lightweight heads to a single-scale backbone feature map, covering words, text lines, and paragraphs, and reconstructs the structural...

papers.title: Time Series Structure Learning with Local Causal Parent Discovery
papers.abstract: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. These challenges complicate the practical application of causal discovery algorithms, which already suffer from high computational and sample complexity in the general case. To mitigate these issues, this work introduces Iterative Temporal Parent Discovery (ITPD): a sound and complete constraint-based procedure for causal structure learning on multivariate time series with causal nonstationarity. ITPD takes a local-to-global learning approach that discovers the global graph by sequentially discovering the parent set for each variable. ITPD exploits temporal structural priors, graph partitioning, and the local Markov condition to swap higher-order conditional independence tests for...

papers.title: UniVEP: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Flow-matching robot policies usually use one prediction target throughout action generation, even though recovering actions from noise and polishing nearly clean actions bring different challenges. We systematically compare velocity prediction (V), endpoint prediction (X), and velocity-weighted endpoint prediction (X--V) across multiple robot policies, benchmarks, and inference budgets. On StarVLA and LiLa-WAM, X--V works best for few-step generation, while V gains more from iterative refinement. We further uncover their complementary strengths across noise levels: clean actions have concentrated covariance spectra, endpoint predictions stay more stable under high noise, and velocity predictions offer more accurate corrections near clean actions. Inspired by these findings, we introduce UniVEP, which learns both prediction targets together with consistency...

papers.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a...

papers.title: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis
papers.abstract: Facial deepfake detectors are usually trained on blending fakes, where a generated face is pasted back into a real frame. Recent generators synthesize the entire face and leave no traces of blending. On a benchmark of 19 datasets released from 2019 to 2026, the best prior facial deepfake detector reaches a mean AUROC of 96.2% on ten blending datasets, but none exceeds 78.1% on five datasets of entire face synthesis (EFS). AI-generated content (AIGC) detectors do not close this gap. We propose TwinD, a detector trained on FaceForensics++ fakes and two kinds of twins: fakes made from a real frame. A reconstruction twin is a real frame reconstructed by an autoencoder, with the real pixels put back in a random region. It targets the neural traces of a decoder. A blob twin blends an altered copy of a real frame with the frame itself, targeting blending artifacts. It...

papers.title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
papers.abstract: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code. In this paper, we study the consequences of directly adopting reasoning-centric training recipes, e.g., the use of outcome-based rewards for reinforcement learning (RL), injection of "cognitive" behaviors such as proposing and backtracking from hypotheses in reasoning chains, etc., for knowledge tasks. We hypothesize that these decisions, while useful for reasoning, inadvertently encourage models to memorize hallucinations they themselves generate in their long reasoning chains when trained on knowledge tasks. To study this, we train models with standard post-training, extract their self-generated hallucinations during RL, and track memorization throughout the rest of training. Our experiments on six open models...

papers.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
papers.abstract: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed of 680 tokens/s using one NVIDIA GB300 GPU at BF16 precision and batch size one. We organize the evaluation around model...

papers.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired....

papers.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
papers.abstract: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding...

papers.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. Multi-view renderings are then used to verify whether the observed behavior satisfies the instruction....

papers.title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark
papers.abstract: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. First, frontier agents outperform AutoML, which reaches less than half the best agent's score, and faithful implementations of published methods on four datasets, of which only 6 of 30 beat the strongest agent's own design; published accuracies, where reproducible, rest on the papers' own conventions, and a single convention,...

papers.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
papers.abstract: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted side decides how much of a request to carry out. We compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands: one sees only the user's words and the command, the information boundary of a reasoning-blind permission classifier, and one also sees the planner's goal and a checked quotation. With gpt-6.1-terra as...

papers.title: Squoosh Bench: Evaluating UX-1 on 318 Historical Website A/B Tests
papers.abstract: Experimentation teams must decide which proposed website changes to test with live traffic. We evaluated whether forecasts from simulated shoppers could inform that choice. We screened 412 historical website A/B tests and evaluated four systems on the 318 that ran longer than 21 days. Each system predicted an original win, a variant win, or an inconclusive result. Page roles were masked and recorded outcomes were withheld during inference. Squoosh UX-1, a model fine-tuned on human browsing data, simulated 1,000 shoppers per arm and correctly classified 267 of 318 outcomes (84.0%, 95% Wilson interval 79.5-87.6%, treating experiments as independent). Qwen3 Next 80B, the strongest general-purpose configuration on outcome accuracy, correctly classified 196 of 318 (61.6%). UX-1 favored the variant in 126 experiments. In the live tests, 118 of those variants won...

papers.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network with interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware. It outperforms gradient-free methods in classification and...

papers.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
papers.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adjust each dimension separately, train Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and evaluate every policy in the original full environment. A...

papers.title: HyCoInfer: Cloud-Edge Collaborative Inference for Large Language Models on Heterogeneous GPU-FPGA Architectures
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving relies predominantly on cloud GPUs, yet autoregressive decoding is memory-bound and often leaves their arithmetic units underutilized. Edge FPGAs offer attractive decoding efficiency, but are ill suited to sustaining a high-concurrency serving workload alone. This paper presents HyCoInfer, a heterogeneous cloud-edge serving system that assigns prefill to cloud GPUs and distributes decoding across cloud GPUs and edge FPGAs. The design addresses three barriers to practical offloading: capacity balancing across heterogeneous accelerators, the large KV cache crossing a constrained wide-area link, and the latency added by heterogeneous execution. HyCoInfer incorporates FPGA decode capacity into GPU prefill/decode role partitioning and places requests according to queue load, prompt length, and network state. It further combines...

papers.title: statLens enables accurate and interpretable statistical intelligence
papers.abstract: Diverse existing approaches and analyses of large-scale biomedical omics datasets along with the complexity of the corresponding statistical analytical workflows pose challenges to the direct application of large language models (LLMs) to data analysis tasks. We present statLens, a model-agnostic AI-driven statistical intelligence framework that integrates LLMs, code and human review. We demonstrate statLens using differential expression analysis across heterogeneous biomedical data as a use case. On 102 benchmark tasks from 74 datasets across six omics modalities, statLens maintained consistently high accuracy (92.5–95.0%) across seven language models and outperformed LLM-only inference (17.5–46.8%), whereas autonomous-agent accuracy varied widely (58.7–99.5%). We also showed that statLens substantially improved the accuracy of the four small language models...

papers.title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching
papers.abstract: Identity matching asks whether two records denote the same identity, yet the answer depends on the target granularity. Two records may match at the base level but not at the variant level: they share an underlying design while differing in attributes such as color or size. Final matching accuracy does not separately characterize the capabilities involved. To study this problem, we use e-commerce as a challenging real-world domain. We introduce PURE, a diagnostic benchmark for multi-granularity multimodal identity matching covering four capability dimensions: Perception, Understanding, Reasoning, and Evidence-grounded Judgment. The benchmark comprises 1,457 multiple-choice questions across 14 tasks, derived from real-world matching pairs and verified by two domain experts. Across ten recent MLLMs, overall scores range from 47.1% to 86.0%. Understanding receives the...

papers.title: Exploited Before It Was Fixed? Vulnerability Timelines from Open, Machine-Readable Evidence
papers.abstract: -05-X-03), Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogs, and exploitation sightings. We introduce an evidence model implemented in Vulnerability-Lookup that selects the earliest evidence for each lifecycle event, distinguishes vulnerability-specific records, preserves date precision, and ensures traceability to original sources. Among 3,758 vulnerability identifiers with exploitation evidence, 98% have disclosure dates, while only 15.7% have patch evidence. Vendor-side dates required by VTEM are entirely absent. Most exploitation dates originate from catalog listings, including 1,041 entries associated with bulk catalog imports. After excluding these entries and ambiguous same-day observations, 59 vulnerabilities exhibit patch evidence following exploitation evidence, with a median interval of 7.6 days, predominantly between catalog listings and distributor...

papers.title: Motion-Aware Reward Modeling for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
papers.abstract: Reward models for instruction-guided video editing can favor temporal consistency at the expense of motion. We study this failure, termed motion collapse, using controlled motion-suppression variants of real edits. On VE-Bench, the evaluated composite reward prefers a motion-suppressed candidate in 97% of cases. Learned video rewards and a VLM judge also struggle with mild suppression, while latent optimization and reward-guided fine-tuning exploit this weakness to increase reward as motion declines. A linear probe of our base reward backbone performs near chance on mild suppression, motivating an explicit inter-frame dynamics input. We propose a motion-aware reward model that combines an RGB frame-difference stream with preference training against motion-suppressed and fabricated-motion negatives. A distillation anchor preserves alignment with human quality...

papers.title: Autoregressive View Model
papers.abstract: We present the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), which generates a scene as a stream of views without constructing an explicit 3D representation. Through a unified in-context interface, AVM conditions on images or videos to generate short clips along a requested camera path. Visual context grounds reconstruction and interpolation, while a learned prior enables extrapolation into unseen regions. AVM retrieves relevant views from inputs and generated history to form a bounded active context. We fine-tune a pretrained bidirectional video diffusion transformer with flow matching in an N-in-1-out formulation. We then tune a causal model on its own rollouts to improve photorealism, reduce denoising steps, and limit long-horizon drift. We scale training to approximately 8M scenes and video clips. We evaluate generation capacity and scene persistence across benchmarks for...

papers.title: MiSTiQ: MicroScaling Trellis Quantization for Extreme KV Cache Compression
papers.abstract: Modern large language models (LLMs) increasingly support longer contexts and serve more concurrent requests, increasing both sequence lengths and batch sizes. Both trends increase KV-cache size and memory traffic during inference. KV-cache quantization reduces these costs, with recent approaches using codebook-based vector quantization to achieve extremely low bit widths. However, hardware constraints limit codebook size, and most methods reconstruct the cache in higher-precision floating-point formats for attention, limiting the computational benefits of quantization. To address these limitations, we introduce MiSTiQ, a drop-in replacement for codebook-based vector quantizers that combines trellis-coded storage with microscaling (MX) formats for low-precision computation. We combine trellis quantization with beam search to encode the KV cache over large...

papers.title: Beyond Bitwidth: Deployment-Constrained Mixed-Precision Quantization for Multilingual LLM Inference on NVIDIA Blackwell
papers.abstract: Low-bit LLM quantization is useful only if a model preserves service-relevant accuracy, executes through supported GPU kernels, and meets measured memory and latency limits. We study Qwen3-8B on NVIDIA B200 with vLLM, including INT2/INT3, GPTQ, NVFP4, and mixed-precision configurations. We verify native packed execution and precision on all 144 fused linear modules and evaluate Korean, English, numerical, and reasoning quality under preregistered gates. Packed INT2 and INT3 execute, but all seven tested INT2 grids degenerate on generation. Isolated module-restoration effects are strongly non-additive; Korean and reasoning sensitivity rankings disagree, and a promising INT4/INT8 development candidate fails independent final evaluation. A configuration with 16-bit activations, 98 NVFP4 weight-only modules, 46 INT8 modules, and an INT8 output head passes all gates on...

papers.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
papers.abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it significantly better. It keeps getting better: it submits an edit only when its own tests support it, each edit replacing the...

papers.title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits
papers.abstract: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. Yet existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit. We introduce ReSpaceBench, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks spanning room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning. Controlled walkthroughs define visits by physical room entry and deliberately include same-type room distractors and cross-session object changes. Our evaluation of 32 models and 3 agentic video-understanding frameworks reveals substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated...

papers.title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
papers.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. Local LLMs hallucinate, and an invented value in a tool call propagates through every later step. Here we present a method to build System 1 agents: local agents that call tools without generating text. A deterministic compiler turns each tool's schema and the request into multiple-choice questions whose options come from the request and the schema, then a one-pass decision model answers them. On 1,952 requests to 157 biomedical tools, the best System 1 agent chose the right tool, or correctly declined, for 97.0% of requests, significantly ahead of all 18 local LLM-agent settings (best 95.2%). The System 1 agent filled 97.0% of 6,056 stated argument values. No System 1 call contained invented...

papers.title: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Agentic LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Key-value (KV) caches impose substantial memory pressure on large language model serving systems, requiring cache eviction when capacity is insufficient. Existing mechanisms typically evict KV from the ends of cached sequences to preserve prefix sharing across requests. However, agent workloads repeatedly reuse long histories across successive turns. Recomputing the KV cache for tokens near the end of a sequence is substantially more expensive than for earlier tokens because their attention computation involves longer histories. To address this problem, we propose preserving shared prefixes and evicting the KV cache from the beginning of the remaining history while retaining the cached suffix. We build Penelope around this strategy by co-designing the eviction policy, KV recomputation, and unified GPU-CPU cache management. Returning requests reuse the KV cache...

papers.title: Quantize, Qualify, Rerank: A Recipe for Compressing LLMs Without Losing Quality
papers.abstract: Compressing large language models lowers serving cost, but a single automatic metric may miss quality loss. For the WMT26 Model Compression constrained track, we compress ‘google/gemma-3-12b-it‘ (24.4 GB in bf16) for three translation directions on one H100. Paired bootstrap analysis exposes metric disagreement on 4-bit quantization; guided by WMT24 human meta-evaluation, we use MetricX24-XXL as primary and CometKiwi-XXL as a cross-check. Removing the unused vision stack and non-task vocabulary and using int8 weights or fp8 activations causes no measurable loss, whereas int4 leaves a small residual. QLoRA healing overfits its calibration domain. A cheap Cometoid best-of-4 reranker at ‘T=0.3‘ improves both the 8-bit and 4-bit systems under held-out CometKiwi-XXL and reference-based MetricX24-XXL. Both surpass greedy bf16 on CometKiwi-XXL; the 8-bit system also...

papers.title: FlashOffloading: Low-Latency KV Cache Offloading for Long-Context LLM Serving
papers.abstract: In large language model (LLM) serving systems, the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with sequence length and concurrency, so long-context inference easily hits the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity wall and results in low concurrency. Offloading the KV cache to host dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) frees HBM space and raises concurrency, but the additional cache management and host-to-device (H2D) load overhead inflates inference latency, higher concurrency fails to translate into effective throughput. We present FlashOffloading, a host-DRAM-centric inference architecture that fully offloads the KV cache in both the prefill and decode phases. FlashOffloading builds rolling HBM cache for prefill, a hot cache for decode, a reverse sparse index with zero extra miss-lookup overhead, and a compute--load overlapped kernel, optimizing KV offloading latency...

papers.title: KVGuard: A KV Cache Safety Checker for LLM Serving Systems
papers.abstract: Modern LLM serving systems manage the KV cache through PagedAttention, a custom GPU allocator that partitions a single CUDA-allocated region into fixed-size physical blocks and maps each request to those blocks through a CPU-built block table. This block-based design exposes a previously unstudied class of memory safety bugs in the KV cache, including double-free, use-after-free, out-of-bounds access, uninitialized read, and permission violation, which silently corrupt outputs or break request isolation without ever crashing the system. Existing memory sanitizers cannot detect them, because they reason about CUDA-level addresses rather than KV cache blocks, requests, and block tables, and their redzone- and quarantine-based designs do not fit the scarce GPU memory budget of LLM serving. This paper presents KVGuard, the first systematic memory-safety abstraction...

papers.title: The Gating Mechanism of KV Cache Eviction
papers.abstract: KV cache eviction must decide which entries carry information that the rest of the cache can no longer supply. A natural way to estimate this is a learnable gate: give each cached entry a gate on its attention weight and train the gate on the model's own objective. The gate belongs inside the normalizing softmax, where suppressing one entry hands its mass to the others rather than discarding it. That same normalizer absorbs any per-query constant, so a constant gate cancels and reproduces the frozen model exactly. Trained on the language-modeling loss the gate stays near a constant score while its loss falls throughout: optimization succeeds, but a frozen backbone was fit for dense attention, so its loss prefers the no-op, and a near-constant score ranks nothing. The no-op is not a floor the gate improves from but what its objective asks for. A second obstacle...

papers.title: TopoSteer: Topological Layer Selection for Activation Steering in LLMs
papers.abstract: Activation steering controls large language models at inference time by adding a vector to their internal representations. Most work asks how to build that vector, and far less attention has gone to where to add it, even though steering at a poorly chosen layer can be worse than not steering at all. Prior selectors choose a layer without ever steering the model to test it: they score how separable the target behavior is at that layer, and how consistently the individual examples point along the steering direction. We argue that what matters is not the separability of the two activation clouds, nor the alignment of individual displacements with their mean, but the extent of the cloud of per-example displacements that mean-difference steering averages. We propose a topology-based layer selection method, called TopoSteer, which scores a layer by the total H_0...

papers.title: From Facts to Personas: Interpretable Role Unlearning in LLMs via Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: LLMs are widely adopted in multi-role dialogue and persona simulation. However, their strong ability to imitate role-specific linguistic and behavioral patterns can introduce privacy risks, reinforce social biases, and lead to unsafe or uncontrollable outputs. To address these issues, we introduce the Role-playing Unlearning task, which aims to selectively forget the style and knowledge associated with target roles while preserving the language ability and behaviors of the remaining roles. Unlike prior unlearning tasks that focus solely on removing factual information, our task additionally requires forgetting persona-specific characteristics, making the control over model generation more fine-grained. We propose RoleMoE, a Mixture-of-Experts framework that maps different roles to more independent expert subspaces, improving role separation and structural...

papers.title: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
papers.abstract: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. We study this distinction in three instruction-tuned models from different families. We construct a one-parameter family of directions ranging from a covariance-adjusted discriminant to the mean difference, and evaluate probing and additive steering, which adds the direction to the hidden state, along the family at a fixed side effect. For truthfulness and sentiment, in every model, the best probe is not the best steering direction: steering consistently favors directions closer to the mean difference. This separation holds across 59 of 60 layer-model-concept combinations in a layer sweep, with...

papers.title: GameWM: Toward Next-Generation Video Games with Interaction-Centric World Models
papers.abstract: For more than half a century, video games have pursued better graphics, more natural interaction, and more engaging gameplay. Generative video models (VMs) now bear on all three. Neural networks already draw most of the pixels in shipped games, and recent world models let a lightweight game engine keep the world state while a VM turns the engine's coarse proxy video into final frames. These systems, however, treat the VM as a renderer that only restyles motion the engine has already authored, which leaves most of its generative capacity unused and limits the diversity a game can offer. We present GameWM, a design for next-generation games built on a clear division of labor. The GameWM-engine keeps what must be exact: rules, state, camera, and the layout of the world, which also spares the video model from having to remember it. The GameWM-VM generates what is...

papers.title: NVFP4-MLA: Unified FP4 KV-Cache Storage and Attention Computation for Multi-Head Latent Attention
papers.abstract: Long-context reasoning and agentic workloads make key-value (KV) cache capacity and attention computation the dominant costs of serving frontier large language models. We present NVFP4-MLA, the first design to push both KV-cache storage and attention computation of multi-head latent attention (MLA) to FP4. NVFP4-MLA co-designs the quantization algorithm with the attention kernel and the cache system. Selective residual compensation preserves model accuracy by adding NVFP4 residuals only to the quantization-sensitive channels. Two-dimensional quantization blocks make the shared latent cache compatible with the different reduction directions of the two attention batched matrix multiplications (BMMs), removing requantization between them. On DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi-K3, NVFP4-MLA matches BF16 MLA average accuracy across nine benchmarks while compressing the MLA KV cache...

papers.title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning
papers.abstract: Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content. Existing methods treat this as a visual restoration problem, yet severely degraded text often cannot be read from local visual evidence alone. Humans instead read it by reasoning over image context, logical patterns, and prior knowledge. This raises a fundamental question: Does TAISR need reasoning? To answer this, we introduce two diagnostic tools. The first, ReasonText, is a human-curated benchmark that separates reasoning-required text from locally recoverable text. The second, Ground-Truth Text-Crop Accuracy (GTTCA), is a recognition-based metric that measures text restoration quality without text detection errors. Evaluating twelve recent super-resolution (SR) models, we find a consistent and substantial performance...

papers.title: Lang-SVG: Hierarchical Image Vectorization with Language Priors
papers.abstract: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. However, most existing vectorization methods optimize for pixel-level render- ing fidelity, often producing SVGs that lack alignment with human-perceived object-part hierarchies, making them difficult to manipulate. To address this, we propose Lang-SVG, which introduces an explicit tree structure to organize SVG primitives with semantic labels and parent-child relationships. Lang-SVG incorporates granularity-controllable and open-vocabulary segmentation priors to initialize object-part hierarchies and leverages multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with SVG tree context to assign semantic labels to unlabeled nodes. To reduce redundancy, we introduce depth-adaptive simplification to reduce shape complexity...

papers.title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Hybrid models combine softmax attention with linear attention, which compresses history into fixed-size recurrent states to balance model quality and inference efficiency. However, linear attention has not pushed this compression to its limit: we find that the queries, keys, and values of linear layers concentrate in a stable, low-dimensional subspace, a phenomenon we call the linear attention sink, so each state is effectively low-rank, with a rank that varies across states. Yet existing serving systems keep these redundant states dense, reading and rewriting them in full at every decoding step, so their memory traffic grows with the batch size and dominates the decoding cost. Thus SinkState stores each recurrent state in an adaptive low-rank form throughout inference with buffered updates and a local SVD restricted to the top subspace. SinkState further...

papers.title: OverlapAdvisor: Modeling and Adapting Computation-Communication Overlap for Distributed MoE Serving
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference with expert parallelism (EP) relies on All-to-All communication, making computation-communication overlap strategies critical for achieving high performance. However, no strategy is universally optimal. Across 103 production configurations, varying input lengths, and four hardware platforms, we observe that the fastest strategy shifts based on model shape, EP degree, input length, and hardware. Since no strategy dominates more than 80.6% of configurations, configuration-aware selection is necessary. In this work, we propose OverlapAdvisor, which models overlap stages using two granularities to capture computation-communication dependencies. OverlapAdvisor builds a unified performance model, accounting for deviations from peak compute, memory, and communication performance across workloads and hardware. This model enables...

papers.title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence
papers.abstract: Optimized floating-point inference is not reproducible across environments: the same model on different hardware, compilers or thread counts can produce different bits. We present tritify, an open-source runtime that executes the forward pass of real models -- decoder-only language models, Mixture-of-Experts decoders, and the Segment Anything 2.1 image/video stack -- with the entire run-time path in exact integer arithmetic; floating point is confined to offline quantization and the float reference used for verification. We make three separate claims and verify each. (1) Cross-hardware reproducibility: the integer path produces bit-identical output run to run, across CPU instruction-set architectures, and across CPU/GPU, carried by a reproducing SHA-256 of the output. (2) Decision fidelity: the integer path reproduces the float reference's decision on the models...

papers.title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood
papers.abstract: Code localizers are usually trained to predict the files a reference patch edits, but the code a fixer needs to read is not the same as the code it changes. We propose Fixer-Guided Localization (FGL): the localizer proposes several localizations, a frozen fixer scores each by how likely it makes a verified patch, and the localizer is trained on these scores with weighted supervised fine-tuning, without running tests and without reinforcement learning. We build the full pipeline on Gemma 4 E4B for the Kaggle Gemma-4 Developer Agent competition, from 1,629 test-verified Kimi K3 trajectories. The FGL target helps the fixer find the bug as often as the teacher's localization while using 27.5% less code. On the development set, one EM round moves the agent in the expected direction compared with a matched control: more tasks reach a patch (53 vs. 46), fewer tasks get...

papers.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
papers.abstract: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. We present BitDecoding-FP4, an algorithm--system co-design for accurate and efficient native FP4 KV decoding. We mitigate three error sources: Dual-Residual Query Quantization splits queries into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; and Outlier-Aware Key...

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Issues in GPU Kernel Libraries for LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Behind the expanding use of large language models (LLMs) across application domains lies a growing dependence on specialized GPU kernel libraries. These libraries underpin the correctness and efficiency of training and inference across diverse GPU platforms, implementing attention, GEMM, quantization, and low-precision operators while managing tensor shapes, memory layouts, code generation, and hardware-specific dispatch. Problems at this layer can silently corrupt outputs, hang GPUs, prevent compilation, introduce deployment incompatibilities, or degrade performance, thereby reducing developer productivity and wasting expensive GPU resources. We present the first comprehensive empirical study of issues in GPU kernel libraries for LLM systems. We manually analyzed 300 high-quality GitHub issue reports, their discussions, and available fixes from seven...

papers.title: FOSCAR: Accelerating Decode Attention over 2- and 4-Bit KV Caches through Affine Folding
papers.abstract: Large-language-model decode attention streams the key-value (KV) cache for every generated token. Packing that cache into 2-bit or 4-bit quantized integers reduces memory traffic but does not automatically translate into latency saving. Existing 2-bit fused kernels reach under 31%/15% of peak HBM throughput on H100/B200. Converting each value and applying its scale and offset before feeding Tensor Cores is a major bottleneck because instruction-issue throughput is scarce on modern GPUs. Instead of applying scale and offset to each KV value, FOSCAR uses affine folding to apply them to the other operand or the output of decode-attention matrix products, depending on the quantization scheme (token-wise or channel-wise). This reduces scale-and-offset operations by up to two orders of magnitude while preserving the dequantized attention output in exact arithmetic....

papers.title: Cross-Layer TopK: Dynamically Allocating Sparsity Across Layers in Transcoders
papers.abstract: Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs) decompose the activations of large language models into human-interpretable features and trace how these features interact across layers to form circuits, making them a key tool for mechanistic interpretability. However, training CLTs effectively and efficiently is hard. Beyond the usual trade-off between sparsity and reconstruction quality, a CLT has to model all layers at once, which adds a further challenge. The common JumpReLU recipe controls sparsity only indirectly through a penalty, while the direct extension of TopK selects a fixed number of latents in every layer. Yet reconstruction difficulty differs widely across layers, and intermediate layers are much harder than others, so giving every layer the same budget is suboptimal. We propose Cross-Layer TopK, which sets a single L0 budget for the whole model and dynamically...

papers.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Quantization reduces the memory and bandwidth demands of large language model (LLM) inference but can degrade accuracy; offloading higher-precision data can instead stall generation. We introduce StrataFlux, a framework that challenges this tradeoff by recovering accuracy lost to low-bit weight and key-value (KV) cache quantization while retaining quantization's memory and speed advantages. StrataFlux co-designs refinement representation, selection, and delivery to make host RAM and solid-state drives useful sources of additional precision. Its selective precision streaming reduces transfer volume, overlaps delivery with computation, and reuses fetched precision across decoding steps so generation need not wait for every transfer. We evaluate 2-4-bit weights and 2-3-bit KV-cache on dedicated GPUs and unified-memory platforms. For 2-bit Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct...

papers.title: ResServe: Accurate and Efficient FP4 LLM Inference with Residue Compensation
papers.abstract: Block-scaled 4-bit floating-point (FP4) quantization reduces large language model inference costs but can degrade task quality. Higher-precision computation can mitigate this loss at the expense of some of the efficiency gains from FP4 inference. Narrow matrix computations common in decoding often leave spare hardware capacity for low-cost precision recovery. ResServe combines an FP4 activation base with an FP4-quantized residue representing information lost during quantization. It uses this spare capacity to compute the residue's contribution and combines results on-chip, avoiding extra result transfers. We apply this principle to linear layers and decode attention, while selective compensation limits added work when processing input prompts. On NVIDIA B200, compensated linear kernels using the NVFP4 format improve numerical precision while retaining latency...

papers.title: GC-MoE: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with FP8/FP4 Grouped GEMM via CUDA Green Contexts
papers.abstract: Under expert parallelism, mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers pay all-to-all token dispatch, grouped GEMMs, and a combine step in every layer. In decode each rank holds only 1-256 tokens: dispatch latency and weight traffic dominate while tensor-core utilization is inherently low. In fused operators such as DeepGEMM's Mega MoE, dispatch and computation overlap only by sharing every SM: dispatch warps compete with TMA/MMA and epilogue warps for registers, shared memory, and issue slots; every phase shares one CTA resource budget, synchronization spans the whole SM array, and every replay ends with a workspace-clean pass and a cross-rank barrier. We present GC-MoE, an open-source FP8/FP4 MoE inference operator for NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs that uses CUDA Green Contexts to split the device into a small communication partition and a large compute partition. Each...

papers.title: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers
papers.abstract: Looped transformers apply a shared block several times per token to improve accuracy without adding parameters. For models such as Ouro that keep a separate key-value (KV) cache per loop, cache memory limits the batch size that amortizes repeated weight reads. Uniform-bit quantization and fixed rules per loop do not allocate precision according to each layer's sensitivity in each loop. Measurements on Ouro show that quantization sensitivity varies across (loop, layer) cells, and the sum of individual cell damages approximates the overall output damage. Sharing damage also varies by cell, with later loops generally tolerating sharing better. Skipping low-attention values to save reads produces errors that compound across loops. LoopKV uses a one-time offline profile to choose 4-bit storage, 2-bit storage or reuse of the final loop's KV for each cell. The planner...

papers.title: FlagRot: Selective Rotation for Low-Bit KV Caches
papers.abstract: Long-context inference is bound by the KV cache, which 2-bit codes could shrink about sixfold if their error stays in check. The usual remedy rotates keys before quantizing, assuming rotation always helps. However, we observe that it does not: rotation flattens a spiky piece of a key but can give a flat one a new peak, and both coexist within one key. We therefore propose FlagRot, which stores each 32-channel piece rotated or as is, whichever has the smaller calibrated attention error, and rotates the query instead when reading. We further show that how often to decide follows the quantization axis: per-channel caches such as KIVI need one decision per head, at no write cost, while per-token caches decide per key, with the choice stored in existing sign bits. At 2.5 bits per value, FlagRot lowers the twelve-model KL divergence of KIVI from 18.7 to 12.4 x 10^-3,...

papers.title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
papers.abstract: Long-horizon reasoning and agentic workloads strain KV-cache capacity and decode attention throughput. We present Jet-QSparse, a training-free method that combines compact NVFP4 cache storage with native FP4 query-key computation on Blackwell tensor cores. A dense scan scores the full key history and selects 128-token blocks for sparse FP16 value aggregation with FP32 accumulation, preserving higher precision in the output-forming step while enabling contiguous tile loads. Calibrated key centering and at most two BF16 pages per sequence and layer address quantization error; FP8 prefill uses a temporary arena while the persistent cache is packed directly from BF16 activations. Across four hybrid LLMs, a budget of 128 blocks per KV head shows no detected accuracy loss on the evaluated mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks, although some smaller...

papers.title: Sparse Autoencoder Attribution Graphs Are Decided at the Margin
papers.abstract: Attribution graphs predict sparse autoencoder (SAE) ablations to first order on the active features, but a TopK SAE passes only its k largest preactivations, so small changes often swap active features. On five public TopK SAEs, zeroing one feature changes the active set of the next layer's SAE in 74% to 89% of cases. Our margin graph adds the first order change to every downstream preactivation, then selects the k largest again. On Pythia-70M the margin graph cuts the median error of predicted activations, relative to their exact change, from the attribution graph's 0.739 to 0.121, 84% lower. Exact recomputation of 48 interventions runs 3.5 times faster than the margin graph on our GPU. Patched into Pythia-70M with the clean reconstruction error, the margin graph's activations predict the change in the subject verb agreement logit difference with 1.95 times the...

papers.title: A Framework for Task-Agnostic Counterfactual Fairness in Transformers through Activation Steering
papers.abstract: Bias in transformer-based models is a growing concern as these architectures become more prevalent in automated decision-making systems, such as prediction models for hiring, lending, and clinical treatment recommendation. Mechanistic interpretability (MI) is a growing body of work that measures meaningful causal effects of activations on model output by identifying human-interpretable features encoded in model activations. When such features correspond to sensitive attributes, they provide a direct way to quantify the bias those attributes introduce and to causally intervene to mitigate it. However, counterfactual fairness (CF) methods have not been systematically adapted to this setting of intervening on interpretable mechanisms in transformers. We propose a framework, Mechanistic Interpretability for Counterfactual Fairness (MICF), that utilizes MI tools to...

papers.title: Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making
papers.abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning remains difficult to interpret and align due to the black-box nature of neural networks. While (neuro-)symbolic approaches improve transparency by incorporating symbolic reasoning, applying them directly to low-level actions results in overly complex, unreadable policies. We introduce NEXUS, a hierarchical RL framework that resolves this tension by combining neural skills with symbolic meta-policies. By shifting transparent reasoning to high-level skills rather than atomic actions, NEXUS drastically reduces symbolic complexity without sacrificing environment performance. Object-centric observations enable high-level reasoning and the design of reward functions and meta-policies by interaction with LLMs. We demonstrate that NEXUS agents learn disentangled skills, are interpretable regarding high-level goals, are better aligned to goals...

papers.title: TriTile: Three-Tier Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Attention over tens of thousands of visual tokens dominates the inference of video diffusion transformers (DiTs). Existing methods reduce this cost through sparsity, low precision, or both, but use a single precision for all kept tiles. We observe that the output error introduced by approximation varies widely across tiles. Many tiles can be skipped with little error, others must be computed but gain little beyond low precision, and a few retain substantial error even at low precision. We present TriTile, a training-free attention method that assigns each tile one of three approximation tiers: skipping it by replacing it with its block means, skimming it in NVFP4, or refining it with NVFP4 residual correction. A lightweight router predicts each tile's error under each tier from block statistics and spends extra compute on a tile only where it removes enough error;...

papers.title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Structure predictors like ESMFold fold proteins using neural network computation and have transformed structural biology. However, the driving mechanism from amino-acid (AA) sequence to 3D structure is insufficiently understood, and biological meaning remains locked in the dense network. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have shown promising results in obtaining interpretable concept features over an overcomplete basis of intermediate protein sequence-model representations. Yet folding models, which predict physical shape from AA sequence semantics, have no such account. We hypothesize that the features carrying the folding computation evolve in the 3D structural regression process. In this paper, we interpret the folding trunk in three steps. First, a pilot analysis on the representation distribution across modules and recycles locates distinct spatial computation in...

papers.title: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
papers.abstract: Automated research is largely evaluated by benchmark performance, but the value of research rarely reduces to a single score. Humans judge a work's holistic contribution through peer review, which is hard to model because it is noisy and depends on many factors. However, what if, given only the paper, we could predict its peer-review decision directly? We introduce PaperScorer, a family of models that predict a paper's accept or reject decision from its extracted text or page screenshots, training only on the decision after removing author identity and formatting shortcuts. Vision models are the most predictive (68% accuracy on ICLR papers and 77% on ML papers from arXiv), beating text-only and frontier reasoning models. Unlike plain text, page images retain figures, layout, and presentation. This signal is robust, surviving smaller models and even compressing the...

papers.title: Racer: Hunting GPU Kernel Bugs with Symbolic Equivalence Checking
papers.abstract: GPU kernels are critical to the performance of today's AI services, yet the same operators are rewritten repeatedly: for each GPU generation, numeric format, serving regime, and kernel language. Every rewrite must preserve the function computed by the implementation it replaces. Today, this obligation depends almost entirely on differential testing: run the new kernel and a trusted reference on randomly sampled tensors, then compare their outputs within a tolerance. This approach has blind spots that additional test cases cannot eliminate. For example, a logical bug may produce an error smaller than the tolerance required to accommodate a correct optimized kernel. We propose symbolic equivalence checking, which executes a kernel and its reference on symbolic inputs, turning each output cell into an exact algebraic expression, and then checks whether the paired...

papers.title: Is 2:4 Sparsity Still Worth It? Semi-Structured Sparsity versus Quantization in LLM Inference
papers.abstract: NVIDIA tensor cores have supported 2:4 semi-structured sparsity since Ampere, and the pattern composes with quantization. When the two are combined, the practical question is which step to take next: from a given precision, add 2:4 sparsity or drop to the next lower precision? We compare the two at equal bits, with sparsity metadata counted, and at equal nominal tensor-core tiers, over all six GEMM operands of a transformer layer, with kernels measured on three GPU generations and online pruning and quantization included. Our results show that as long as a lower precision is available, adding 2:4 is the worse step, both less accurate and slower, because the energy that 2:4 discards from each group of four along the hardware-forced axis does not shrink with bits, while quantization error does. Once quantization reaches the lowest precision the hardware supports,...

papers.title: RealControlBench: A Benchmark for Interpretability-Informed Fine-Grained Control of LLMs and Agents
papers.abstract: Existing steering benchmarks are built around simplified, isolated generation tasks and evaluate a single behavioral attribute under controlled settings that do not reflect the diversity and complexity of practical deployment. As a result, performance on these benchmarks provides only a limited picture of how steering methods perform in the real world. We therefore introduce RealControlBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating fine-grained steering of LLMs and LLM agents across diverse behavioral targets and interaction settings. RealControlBench extends steering evaluation beyond isolated generations to complex, execution-grounded, multi-turn agent interactions, covering five complementary dimensions: instruction-following control, agentic tool-use decision control, reasoning-performance steering, reasoning-length control, and trajectory-conditioned safety...

papers.title: PACT: NVFP4 Data-Flow LoRA Fine-Tuning on Consumer GPUs
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning language models on consumer GPUs is constrained by computation and memory. Although LoRA reduces trainable parameters and optimizer state, frozen projections remain expensive, and activations retained for backward can dominate memory usage. We present PACT, a LoRA fine-tuning system that accelerates frozen projections with native NVFP4 GEMMs while reducing quantization and dequantization overhead and limiting quantization error. To reduce activation memory, PACT reuses quantized RMSNorm outputs and saves gate/up activations in NVFP4 for backward. To limit numerical error, it preserves BF16 inputs for forward nonlinear operations and calibrates frozen weights offline using GPTQ adapted to NVFP4 scales and quantized activations. Fused nonlinear kernels and cached forward and backward weight layouts reduce quantization and dequantization overhead....

papers.title: Comparing Sparsified MLPs and Transcoders: Many Transcoder Features Are Neurons in Disguise
papers.abstract: MLP neurons in transformer language models are widely understood to be polysemantic, motivating transcoders - sparse, learned approximations of MLP layers - as interpretable replacement models for mechanistic analysis. However, recent work shows that MLP neurons can be used to recover sparse, interpretable circuits (Arora et al. 2026, Ye et al. 2025), raising the question of whether transcoders are necessary for circuit analysis. We define neuron features as transcoder features whose weights are strongly aligned with individual MLP neurons, and show that they account for a substantial fraction of active features in late layers across 13 open-source transcoders. Only neuron features have a stable correspondence with something in the underlying MLP: other features vary more between training runs, do not match the MLP's Jacobian, and change less significantly from...

papers.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
papers.abstract: Understanding and simulating how subjective cognition and mental states emerge, evolve, and shape behavior is essential for advancing artificial intelligence toward deeper social cognition and general intelligence. Existing large language models (LLMs) and Theory of Mind (ToM) methods primarily infer mental states from linguistic information, lacking unified mechanisms for subjective world construction, cognitive-psychological interactions, dynamic evolution, and historical dependencies. This paper introduces the Mental World Model (MWM) and its implementation, the Multi-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture (MMEA), which explicitly constructs subjective worlds, models interactions between cognition and mental states, and simulates continuous mental evolution shaped by historical experiences. On DynToM and RecToM, MMEA achieves 96.48% and 94.00% accuracy,...

papers.title: A Self-Pruning Transformer: Extreme KV-Cache Compression with Universal Attention
papers.abstract: The large KV-cache size of modern LLMs creates a barrier to efficient deployment. Recent work has explored replacing attention layers' RoPE positional embeddings with alternative decay-based mechanisms, which can then be used to prune KV-cache during inference. However, these decay functions have limited expressivity, and in practice devolve into sliding-window-like eviction patterns. In this work, we propose a unifying framework for complementary and novel decay mechanisms, capturing complex key statistics and interactions while preserving expressive RoPE embeddings and Softmax attention. The resulting Universal Attention is a highly expressive and end-to-end trainable architecture, whose composite decay mechanism acts as a natural, $\textit{adaptive}$ pruning criterion, removing tokens that contribute least to attention computation. Experimentally, Universal...

papers.title: Behavior-Preserving KV Cache Compression
papers.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
papers.abstract: KV caches are a major bottleneck in long-context inference and long-form generation with large language models. Existing training-free eviction policies largely rely on proxy importance signals, such as attention mass, to decide which past tokens to retain. We argue that cache compression should instead preserve the predictive behavior of the full-cache model, retaining entries whose removal would substantially change the model’s output distribution. We propose Behavior-Preserving KV Cache Compression, a training-free framework that scores candidate evictions by estimating the compressed-cache logits induced by their removal and evaluating the resulting KL to the full-cache next-token distribution. Using pre-eviction forward statistics, the method avoids running separate masked forward passes for each candidate. Across diverse architectures and both prefill-time...

papers.title: Monte Carlo Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
papers.abstract: Most KV-cache eviction methods ask, in effect, which memory appeared important while reading the prompt? We instead ask which memory will matter while answering? Since decoding queries are unavailable at eviction time, prior future-aware methods rely on pseudo-responses or synthetic future-query estimates. We cast fixed-budget future-aware eviction as distributional estimation over plausible model-conditional query trajectories and introduce LORE-KV (Lookahead Output-perturbation with Reliability-weighted Ensembles for Key-Value caches), a training-free method that samples short autoregressive continuations from the frozen target model and uses their response-side query states to estimate prompt-token utility. Tokens are scored by projected leave-one-out attention-output deletion cost and aggregated across sampled futures with optional trajectory weighting. The...

papers.title: Secure Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates inference for a large language model (LLM), referred to as the \emph{target model}, by first using a smaller model, referred to as the \emph{draft model}, to generate candidate tokens and then verifying them with the target model for acceptance or rejection.
